St. Xenia of Saint Petersburg

Saints

St. Xenia of Saint Petersburg

Period
Eighteenth century; precise dates not established here
Region
Russia
Titles / vocation
Fool-for-Christ · Woman · Lay
Commemoration
January 24

Introduction

St. Xenia is remembered as a widow and Fool-for-Christ in Saint Petersburg. The OCA life explicitly notes the limited information about her early life and family. It describes her bereavement, renunciation of possessions, and life among the city's people, followed by veneration at her grave. The profile preserves those documentary limits rather than supplying precise unsupported birth and death dates.

Read circumstances and sources

Background

Xenia lived in eighteenth-century Saint Petersburg. She was married to an army officer named Andrew and was widowed at twenty-six.

[2] Ecclesiastical history or testimony · GOARCH January 24 reading; marriage and widowhood

Life and notable events

She adopted her husband’s name and military clothing and lived without a settled home. The church account describes this as foolishness for Christ: she endured ridicule, accepted little for herself, helped poor people, and secretly carried bricks for a church being built in the Smolensk cemetery. Accounts of prophecy and healing belong to the devotional tradition surrounding her.

[1] Ecclesiastical saint’s life · Published life; biographical narrative, source anchor “bricks”

The Greek Archdiocese’s reading preserves a period of eight years during which Xenia was absent from Saint Petersburg. It presents a stay in a hermitage as a belief about that interval, rather than an established itinerary. The same reading places her return in her husband’s military clothing before describing her wandering life and prayer for him.

[2] Ecclesiastical history or testimony · GOARCH January 24 reading; absence and return to Saint Petersburg

Death and martyrdom

Her precise death date and its circumstances are not known. The published life places her repose near the end of the eighteenth century and her burial in Smolensk cemetery.

[1] Ecclesiastical saint’s life · Published life; biographical narrative, source anchor “exact date”

Writings and legacy

Veneration developed around her grave and the chapel later built there.

[1] Ecclesiastical saint’s life · Published life; biographical narrative, source anchor “chapel”
